title: Losing someone
hookLine: to Allah we belong and to Him we return (2:156)
tomorrow: after a funeral, what's actually useful?

cards: A gentle note for parents: today is about a death. A text that just says: she passed, an hour ago. Thumbs hover.
Every reply looks wrong. Sorry for your loss feels like a form letter, and anything longer feels like too much. What do you say in the first moment, before there's time to think?
Muslims have words ready for exactly that moment, and they come straight from the Qur'an. A friend of another faith may arrive with words of her own, surprisingly close.

teach.b: In Surah al-Baqarah, God says people will be tested with loss, of wealth and lives and the fruits of their work, and gives good news to the steadfast, who say, in Pickthall's words, when a misfortune strikes them: "Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning."
In Arabic: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un. Two halves. We are Allah's: the person we lost was never ours to keep; they were His, and lent to us for a while.
Unto Him we are returning: all of us, the one who died and the ones left at the graveside. It isn't only goodbye. It's a statement of where everyone is headed.
The next verse says blessings and mercy from their Lord are on the people who say it. Now a neighbor.

teach.h: JOB: THE LORD GAVE, AND HATH TAKEN.
teach.b: In the Hebrew Bible, read by Jews and Christians, Job loses everything, his children too, and says, in an older Jewish translation: "the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD."
The old Book of Common Prayer reads it at Christian burials. What's shared: what we had was given, and not ours to hold forever.

teach.h: ONE LOOKS BACK, ONE LOOKS AHEAD.
teach.b: One honest difference: Job's line looks back, blessing God for both the giving and the taking.
The ayah looks ahead, to where we're going: back to Him.

how: On hearing of a death or any loss, Muslims say inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un; the community washes and shrouds the body, prays the janazah prayer, buries quickly, and visits and feeds the bereaved family.

o: a loss that shows God has turned away from you
a loss best handled by not speaking of the person
a loss met with: we are Allah's, and we return to Him

games.q: what goes with what — tap the pairs.
p: the one we lost was His, not ours
all of us, not only the one who died
the LORD gave, and hath taken away

s: inna lillahi is only for when someone dies
the ayah names any misfortune that strikes, not only a death.
'unto Him we are returning' includes the people left behind
returning is for all of us: the one who died and the ones who grieve.

games.q: a classmate posts that her grandfather died last night. what words does the ayah give for that first moment?
o: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un: we are Allah's, and to Him we return.
alhamdulillah: praise God, he's surely in a better place now.
insha'Allah: if God wills, things will start to get better soon.
games.why: 2:156 gives the words for the moment a misfortune strikes. the next verse says blessings and mercy are on those who say them.

practice: Close your eyes and bring to mind someone you've lost, recently or long ago. Say their name, silently.
If you pray, you can ask Allah's mercy and forgiveness for them, as Muslims do at a janazah; if not, hold their name, and a thank-you for the time you had.

wordCard.voice: Losing someone: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un. We are Allah's, and to Him we are returning.

orig.say: IN-naa lil-LAAHI wa IN-naa i-LAY-hi raa-ji-OON
orig.note: Arabic (2:156): we are Allah's, and to Him we are returning.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: we return, all of us, to the One who lent them to us. Go gently today.
